chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Custom OBJ Button
chunks.content: ## Preparing and Positioning the Flower Model in CLO This section explains how to correctly position a flower model in CLO, focusing on the importance of origin placement and export settings for optimal button integration. - Open or create a flower model, ensuring it is placed precisely at the origin in the 3D window. - The origin is identified by two vertical lines on the floor at the midpoint of the x-axis and y-axis. - The flower must be flat on the floor at the origin because this point determines where the custom button will point upward on the board. - Proper alignment at the origin also ensures consistent axis directions when exporting. ## Exporting the Model to OPT Format This section covers the steps and options for exporting the flower model as an OPT file, which is necessary for importing into CLO’s button materials system. - Export the model to OPT format by naming the file and clicking Save. - In the export window: - Choose "All Panels." - Select "Single Target" to export the entire flower as one object. - Do not select “Unified UV Coordinates” because the flower has no texture. - Do not save flag colors since the flower is white with no texture. - Save the file as a compressed ZIP package, which will include the OPT and any texture files (if applicable). - Avoid the option for multiple targets as it will split the flower into many smaller grids, complicating selection and manipulation later. ## Extracting and Importing the OPT File into CLO This section outlines how to extract the zipped OPT file and import it into CLO’s button creation system. - Extract the compressed ZIP package to access the OPT file. - In CLO, add a new button and use the plus sign to connect multiple button materials. - Click the browse button, then open the extracted OPT file. - If multiple targets were exported, select all grids; however, single target export simplifies management. - When multiple grids appear, navigating between them becomes complex due to numerous flower parts. - Naming the object (e.g., "Airline") helps organize the materials and selections. ## Adjusting Button Dimensions and Axis Alignment This section details how to adjust the button’s size and thickness to maintain proportionality and prevent deformation, based on measurements in millimeters. - Adjust the button width according to the flower’s size; for example, set width to 10 mm. - Set the bottom thickness proportionally (e.g., thickness 4 mm) to preserve the shape. - Example: width 15 mm corresponds with thickness 6.2 mm. - Since the model was placed at the origin when exported, axis alignment is already correct, so no further axis conversion is necessary. - Confirm the settings to finalize the size and placement. ## Applying Twist Tool for Material and Color Effects This section explains how to use CLO’s twist tool to enhance the button’s appearance by applying twists based on material and color. - Use the move twist tool within CLO.
